Rafiqul Huq with Md Azizul Hoque, Faheemul Huq, Ahsanul Karim, Advocates -----For the Petitioner.

parties:
Tasmima Hossain ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Anti-Corruption Commission represented by its Chairman and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
MA Rashid J: The above Rule Nisi was issued asking the respondent Anti-Corruption Commission to show cause as to why initiation and continuation of proceedings of ACC GR Case No. 125 of 2007 corresponding to Dhanmondi PS Case No. 20 of 2007 dated 7-10-07 then pending before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Dhaka should not be declared to have been initiated and continued without any lawful authority and, as such, of no legal effect and as to why the rule 15ঘ of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 should not be declared to be ultra vires of the Emergency Powers Ordinance, 2007 and the Constitution. 

 5. Definite case of the petitioner is that no notice under section 26 of the ACC Act and/or rule 15X of the EP Rules, 2007 was ever served upon the petitioner. 

 6. Respondent No. 1, Chairman on behalf of the Commission, appeared and filed an affidavit-in-opposition opposing the Rule. In the affidavit, it is stated that the petitioner on 17-6-2007 submitted the statements of assets of her husband Anwar Hossain before the Commission. After investigation, a charge sheet was submitted. Upon receipt of the charge-sheet, the Metropolitan Senior Magistrate Judge took cognisance of offences against the petitioner and her husband. Then, he sent the case to the competent Court of Special Judge for trial and the trial is going on. But no necessary particulars of such proceedings were provided in the affidavit. 

 9. He submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the case, lodging of the first information report and initiation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioner in connection with service of notice under section 26 of the ACC Act and/or rule 15ঘ(5) of the EP Rules, 2007 upon her husband was malafide, motivated and, as such, illegal. 

 26. It appears that the writ petition was moved at the instance of a constituted attorney of the petitioner and the Rule was obtained on 7-1-2008. On that day the petitioner was admittedly never asked by any court or any process to appear before any Court or Tribunal in connection with any case. A 'fugitive from justice' cannot be allowed to seek any redress or remedy under the criminal administration of justice. But such concept 'fugitive from justice', we are afraid could be pressed into operation or resorted to in respect of an application made under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

 A Division Bench of this Division in the case of Shafiqul Islam Shimul held that— 

 "Moreover, an action taken without lawful authority can be challenged, according to us, by an aggrieved person on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, and the criminal case against him, if any, or non appearance in the said criminal case shall not, according to us, debar him from seeking justice in this forum under Article 102 of the Constitution." 

 28. In the case, the petitioner who did not appear in a criminal case under the Arms Act, 1878 challenged an action of the authority canceling his licence to possess arms and ammunition. 

 29. In the cases of Mansur Ali and Alamgir relied upon by Md Khurshid Alam Khan, leave was refused by the Appellate Division against orders of this Division passed in revision and miscellaneous case for quashing against conviction and sentence refraining from interfering with the orders of lower Court since the accused were found to be fugitive from justice as they were not in custody after conviction and sentence. There cannot be two opinions on such decision but such authority would be of no help for the Commission in the case before us. 

 30. For the reasons aforesaid, in the first information report or in the proceedings initiated upon such first information report no offence was ever disclosed against the petitioner and, as such, initiation of the case by lodging a first information report against the petitioner must be held to be unauthorised, without jurisdiction and malefide. 

 32. First information report being No. 20 of 2007 dated 7-10-07 lodged with Dhanmondi Police Station corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 125 of 2007 and further proceedings, if any, upon such first information report are all declared to have been lodged, initiated and continued against the petitioner without lawful authority and, as such, of no legal effect and accordingly, quashed so far the petitioner is concerned.
